target: AArch64 native ZealC on PCI QEMU

checks.evidence: The installed Wallpaper Desktop Palette icon launched the editor. The random-color key changed palette entry 0 and scanout. The # hex-entry path accepted 123456; the live entry's R/G/B channels were 18/52/86 and scanout changed. Escape closed the editor, retained the edited value, and the terminal recovered with 40+2=42.

The combined test also passed the installed desktop, all six controls, focused Home and Terminal shells, Stats toggle, NetLog open/write/close/reopen, and Telnet form, local fixture connection, typed input, socket close, and task exit.

scope_note: Automated disposable-disk QEMU acceptance only. It covers Palette Editor random-color and hex-entry workflows, opening the filename form, returning from it with Escape, exiting the editor, and terminal recovery. Successful save persistence, opening a saved palette, arbitrary HomeSys customization, and live UTM/Pi desktop behavior remain unverified. The application remains partial in the source ledger because its full workflow and host-specific live coverage are not complete.

save_as_follow_up.result: pass for filename-form Escape and guest recovery
save_as_follow_up.steps: From the installed Wallpaper Desktop, open Palette Editor, change a color, enter Ctrl+A, then press Escape in the filename form.
save_as_follow_up.observed: The FileName form rendered. Escape returned without an unresolved external call; a second Escape closed the editor, and the terminal accepted the recovery expression (40+2=42). The test did not inspect whether a palette file was created or verify its contents.
save_as_follow_up.target: AArch64 native ZealC on PCI QEMU, disposable disk
save_as_follow_up.source_change: The source bundle now includes the pinned portable StrFind and StrReplace implementations used by PESave. DoNothing's unresolved imported-call decoder now searches the full supported load sequence, which reports the actual missing symbol when one remains.
